findings.body: The panel reduces every refusal to its HTTP status and therefore displays the wrong reason for several route outcomes. For example, the unchanged Ask drill service returns 403 with “This answer link is invalid…” for a tampered signature and 403 with the access-changed wording for another user, while this branch maps both to the access-changed message. Likewise, all 409 responses are presented as missing data even though the route also uses 409 for footing mismatches and incomplete pins. Preserve a typed refusal reason/message from `/api/chat/drill` instead of guessing from status alone.

findings.body: The refusal test injects synthetic errors directly into `DrillPanel` and asserts locally hard-coded status text. It never reaches `/api/chat/drill`, so it cannot catch transport-envelope handling (including the incorrect status-only mapping), authentication/authorization changes, expiry, or audit-failure behavior in the browser. Done-when item 7 therefore remains without the required real-entry-point Playwright proof.
